newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Refugio gold pit still shut, miners leave.
newsitem.headline: Chile Refugio gold pit still shut, miners leave.

text.p: Around 100 miners have been evacuated by helicopter from the Refugio gold mine in northern Chile which has been closed for more than two weeks by heavy snowfall, said a mine official.
"Between yesterday and today we have evacuated all the people at Refugio using four helicopters," said human resources manager Anibal Avendano.
"We have only left behind the people strictly necessary to do maintenance work at the mine."
The miners have been stranded at the pit's base camp since mid-June when blizzards cut access roads to Refugio which lies high in the Andes 4,700 meters above sea level.
The bad weather has slashed gold production at the mine owned equally by Bema Gold Corp and Amax Gold, said an official at the pit.
"In the whole month we have not even produced 3,000 ounces of gold," said the official.
Refugio usually produces around 20,000 ounces of gold a month.
Work to clear the road is progressing slowly as the result of high winds which have whipped snow into drifts over five meters deep in places, said Avendano.
Around 50 kilometers of the road have still to be cleared and the road to the mine could be reopened in the next 2-3 days, he said.
